# EASA feedback-element trade-off (generated by `02_EASA/scripts/easa_tradeoffs.py`; do not edit)

Scope: alert system only; the latch is not changed. RF = reduction of the per-flight probability of taking off with the canopy not locked and nothing effective done, against no system. *Acts* = the pilot acts on every alert he notices; *matches* = he acts as often as alerts have been right (probability matching). Cue detection combined as independent (upper) or fully dependent (lower bound, the best single cue). Fatal = fatal outcomes per flight from canopy openings plus engine losses the device causes. Inputs: `02_EASA/inputs/inputs.json` and `cues.json` (source and tag per value). [K] unless marked.

**Design decisions (user, 5 Nov 2026):** no mechanical restriction on the throttle lever (a jammed or wrongly engaged restriction is a serious risk in flight), and no vibration on the throttle knob (a vibration source on a primary engine control; CS 23.1141(c) 'tendency to creep due to ... vibration'; research/R10). The vibration cue moves to a lap-belt tactor. The recommended set is **O5** (dedicated lamp + voice "CANOPY, CANOPY" + taxi chime + lap-belt tactor, lever-switch trigger). The knob shaker (O5k), the take-off gate (O6, O6p/n/m), the cable throttle pawl (O9) and the starter guard (O10) stay as compared and rejected options; engine shut-down (O7, O8) was already rejected. O6 to O10 now build on the belt set.

## 1. Sensing (Monte Carlo, 200000 flights per cell, seed 2026)

Each cell: observed count / flights → estimate, and the 95 % Wilson upper bound. **A zero count is not a zero probability**: it only bounds the probability (≈ 3/n). The false-alert column adds the separate nuisance rate of `inputs.json` (3e-4 per flight, [Y]); the sensor model alone produced the counts shown.

| Architecture | Miss: partial lock | Miss: one bolt out | Miss: not seated | Sensor-model alerts with no hazard | False + nuisance per 1 000 flights |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No system (pilot check only) | 1 (no system) | 1 | 1 | — | 0 |
| One microswitch at one pin, plain contact (organisers' example) | 171/200000 → 0.00085 (≤ 0.001) | 133345/200000 → 0.67 (≤ 0.7) | 1/200000 → 5e-06 (≤ 3e-05) | 0/200000 → 0 (≤ 2e-05) | 0.30 |
| Seated + all three bolts, self-checking | 87/200000 → 0.00044 (≤ 0.0005) | 103/200000 → 0.00052 (≤ 0.0006) | 0/200000 → 0 (≤ 2e-05) | 2/200000 → 1e-05 (≤ 4e-05) | 0.31 |

## 5. Multi-criteria comparison

Computed criteria [K]: *effectiveness* = log RF (acts), *distrust robustness* = log RF (matches, mean of both bounds), each scaled to the best option; *no new hazard* = 1 − (engine-loss fatalities the device adds ÷ fatalities with no system). Judgement criteria [Y]: the table after this one gives the reason for every score. Weights resampled 20 000 times (Dirichlet, concentration 20).

**Reasons for the judgement scores [Y]:**

| Option | What one false alert costs the pilot | Works on any canopy type, with or without EFIS, intercom or engine | Parts, wiring and set-up work | Worst credible failure of the device itself |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O0 | 1.00: no alerts | 1.00: nothing to fit | 1.00: none | 1.00: no device |
| O1 | 1.00: no alerts | 0.80: needs a view of each latch point | 0.80: paint bands; a window may be needed | 0.90: a mis-painted band |
| O2 | 0.70: message + tone; plain switches flicker under flight loads (Van's notes, RV-14) | 0.40: needs an EFIS with a canopy discrete | 0.90: one switch, one wire, EFIS set-up | 0.30: short to ground or a mis-set switch reads LOCKED (RV-14, fatal) |
| O3 | 0.90: a lamp only | 0.90: standalone lamp | 0.60: 4 sensors, harness, unit, lamp | 0.80: self-checking; false green only for two double faults |
| O4 | 0.75: lamp + voice | 0.80: needs an audio input (most gliders have none) | 0.55: + audio panel input | 0.80: as O3 |
| O5 | 0.65: lamp + voice + vibration | 0.80: needs a lap belt only | 0.50: + belt tactor and a lead along the harness | 0.80: as O3; a dead tactor is reported amber; nothing touches the engine controls |
| O6 | 0.45: a stop at the holding point and a release action | 0.45: needs a throttle quadrant and air/ground sensing | 0.30: + solenoid detent, IAS/GPS inputs | 0.65: detent jam in flight, mitigated by a mechanical breakout |
| O7 | 0.25: the engine stops; restart needed | 0.35: needs ignition access; not for gliders | 0.35: + ignition interface | 0.30: a logic fault cuts the engine in the air |
| O8 | 0.00: the engine stops in flight | 0.30: as O7 | 0.35: as O7 | 0.10: every false alert in flight cuts the engine |
| O9 | 0.45: a stop at the holding point and a release action | 0.50: needs a throttle and cable runs; no electrics needed | 0.35: cable runs from three lugs to the quadrant, rigged against 60 mm partial lock | 0.50: cable slack misses a partial lock; no ground/air logic, blocks re-advance in the air |
| O10 | 0.40: canopy must be locked to start, then may be reopened for taxi | 0.55: needs a starter; not for pure gliders | 0.45: plunger cable to a flap at the starter | 0.85: fails only to prevent a start; must never cover the OFF direction |

## 7. Do the sensor failure-rate assumptions matter? (review 5 Nov, problem 3)

The rates in `inputs.json` transfer an industrial NAMUR sensor FMEDA with a MIL-HDBK-217F switch environment factor; they are not an Extra NG installation rate. This table reruns the A3 sensing Monte Carlo with the rates changed. Misses are set by rigging scatter and the common mis-rig, not by random sensor failure, so the RF barely moves until the rates are raised a hundredfold. Fault cautions of 0 mean none in 200 000 flights (below the Monte Carlo resolution of ≈ 1.5e-5), not zero.

| Scenario | Miss: partial | Miss: one bolt | Fault cautions per flight | O4 acts / matches | O5 acts / matches | O6 (rejected) acts / matches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| as in inputs.json (NAMUR FMEDA × πE 18, shorts 0) | 0.00044 | 0.00052 | 0.0e+00 | 23.5× / 2.7× | 71.3× / 2.8× | 1 175× / 16.3× |
| no environment factor (rates ÷ 18) | 0.00044 | 0.0005 | 0.0e+00 | 23.5× / 2.7× | 71.3× / 2.8× | 1 179× / 16.3× |
| every rate × 10 | 0.00044 | 0.00062 | 5.0e-06 | 23.5× / 2.7× | 71.2× / 2.8× | 1 154× / 16.0× |
| every rate × 100 | 0.00044 | 0.0014 | 3.5e-05 | 23.4× / 2.6× | 70.7× / 2.7× | 1 019× / 14.6× |
| shorts added at the open-circuit rate × 10 | 0.00044 | 0.00052 | 0.0e+00 | 23.5× / 2.7× | 71.3× / 2.8× | 1 175× / 16.3× |
| latent check every 1 000 h instead of 100 h | 0.00044 | 0.00062 | 0.0e+00 | 23.5× / 2.7× | 71.2× / 2.8× | 1 154× / 16.3× |
